emotionInsights.happy: Your voice conveys joy and energy – a strong sign of wellbeing. Positive emotions strengthen your resilience and nourish your relationships.
emotionInsights.sad: Your voice carries a certain weight and sorrow. It's completely okay – grief is an important part of being human and helps us process loss. You don't have to carry it alone.
emotionInsights.anxious: Your voice shows signs of worry and inner tension. Your brain is trying to protect you – but worry can sometimes become disproportionate. You're not alone with this, and it can be managed.
emotionInsights.angry: Your voice carries intense energy suggesting frustration or anger. Anger is a signal that something important has been violated – it's human. It's about channeling it constructively.
emotionInsights.fearful: Your voice shows signs of fear or great worry. Fear is the body's alarm system – but sometimes it overreacts. If you're in danger or feeling very unwell: seek help now.
emotionInsights.neutral: Your voice sounds balanced and neutral. It could indicate calm and wellbeing – or that you're holding back emotions. Sometimes it's harder to reach the deeper layers.
emotionInsights.surprised: Your voice shows surprise or unexpected engagement. Surprise is often fleeting – notice what created it.
emotionInsights.disgusted: Disgust or aversion in the voice can signal that something conflicts with your values. It's important information about your boundaries.
emotionInsights.frustrated: Frustration is a signal of an obstacle or inequity. It's an active emotion that says: "Something isn't right." Listen to it with curiosity.

happy: Enjoy the moment – notice what created the joy
Share your energy with someone you care about
Write down three things you're grateful for today
sad: Allow yourself to feel, don't flee the emotion
Breathe deeply: in 4 sec → hold 2 sec → out 6 sec
Call someone you trust – a conversation helps
anxious: 4-7-8 breathing: in 4 sec → hold 7 sec → out 8 sec
Grounding technique: Name 5 things you see, 4 you hear, 3 you touch
Ask yourself: How likely is this scenario really?
angry: Box breathing: in 4 → hold 4 → out 4 → hold 4 sec
Take a step back and count to 10 before reacting
Move around – a quick walk lowers stress hormones
fearful: If in immediate danger: Call 112 immediately
Grounding technique: Press your feet into the floor, breathe slowly
neutral: Reflect: How are you really feeling deep inside?
Mindfulness: Sit still for 5 minutes and observe your thoughts
Write down your thoughts in a journal
surprised: Consider: What surprised you and what does it say about your expectations?
Curiosity is positive – let surprise lead to exploration
disgusted: Communicate your boundaries clearly and respectfully
Is there something you need to distance yourself from?
frustrated: Identify the specific obstacle: what can you control?
Break the problem into smaller parts
Move around – physical activity dissolves frustration thinking

catastrophizing.label: Catastrophizing
catastrophizing.hint: The thought predicts the worst possible outcome without middle-ground scenarios.
catastrophizing.reframeQuestion: What is the most likely outcome, not the worst?

black_white.label: Black-and-white thinking
black_white.hint: The thought uses extremes like "always", "never" or "completely".
black_white.reframeQuestion: What more nuanced middle ground could be true?

mind_reading.label: Mind reading
mind_reading.hint: The thought assumes what others think without clear evidence.
mind_reading.reframeQuestion: What actual evidence do you have for what others are thinking?

self_labeling.label: Global self-labeling
self_labeling.hint: A mistake is turned into a general label about you as a person.
self_labeling.reframeQuestion: How would you describe the situation without labeling yourself?

noData.title: Continued reflection
noData.message: You have done important work. Continued repetition of the balanced thought can make it more accessible in everyday life.

clearRestructuring.title: Clear restructuring
clearRestructuring.message: Your new thought feels considerably more credible now. This indicates you have broken an automatic stress interpretation pattern.

goodProgress.title: Good progress
goodProgress.message: You are moving in the right direction. Keep practicing the new thought in similar situations to consolidate the effect.

stabilization.title: Stabilization needed
stabilization.message: Change takes time. Try to concretize the evidence further and try the same exercise again in a calm moment.

noData.title: Stress measurement missing
noData.message: Add stress level before and after next time to more clearly see the effect of the exercise.

clearReduction.title: Clear stress reduction
clearReduction.message: Your stress level dropped significantly. Continue with the same strategy in similar situations.

goodRegulation.title: Good stress regulation
goodRegulation.message: Stress level decreased. Repeat the remaining action steps to consolidate the effect.

remaining.title: Stress partially remains
remaining.message: If stress is still high, combine the thought with a short breathing pause before the next step.

clinicalAssessment.title: Clinical Self-Assessment
clinicalAssessment.subtitle: Validated scales for depression (PHQ-9) and anxiety (GAD-7)

phq9Questions.little_interest: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
phq9Questions.sleep_problems: Trouble falling asleep, or sleeping too much
phq9Questions.feeling_tired: Feeling tired or having little energy
phq9Questions.feeling_bad: Feeling bad about yourself or that you are a failure
phq9Questions.moving_slowly: Moving or speaking slowly, or being restless
phq9Questions.self_harm: Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself

gad7Questions.feeling_nervous: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
gad7Questions.cant_control_worry: Not being able to stop or control worrying
gad7Questions.worrying_too_much: Worrying too much about different things
gad7Questions.restless: Being so restless that it's hard to sit still
gad7Questions.afraid: Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen
